blocks.text: In 1809 Lamarck published 'Philosophie Zoologique' (Zoological Philosophy), presenting the idea of progressive change now called Lamarckism. His proposed mechanism had two parts.

items: Use and disuse of organs: when an organism's environment changes it uses some organs more and others less; organs used more develop and become strong, and those not used deteriorate. Lamarck called such changes, caused by long use or disuse, acquired characters.

Inheritance of acquired characters: characters acquired during an organism's life are passed to its offspring; inherited over generations, they modify organisms to cope better with changes in the environment.

blocks.text: According to Lamarckism, the ancestors of giraffes had short necks and ate grass or the leaves of small plants. When small plants were no longer available, some individuals began stretching their necks to reach the leaves of tall trees; their necks became stronger and longer during their lives, an acquired character. Their offspring were born with slightly longer necks, kept stretching, and over many generations long-necked giraffes evolved.

blocks.alt: Four giraffes in three shaded zones with leafy branches above. Short-necked ancestor: a short-necked giraffe below a branch it cannot reach. Necks became long as a result of stretching: a giraffe with a longer neck stretching to the leaves. Acquired characters passed to next generations: two giraffes with still longer necks reaching higher branches. Red arrows lead from each giraffe to the next.
